AgentRegistryEntry.description: One registered agent kind, returned by `GET /registry/agents`.

supported_games.description: Registered game ids this agent kind supports. Empty means "game-agnostic" (usable with any game).

ApiError.description: Uniform error body, shared by every endpoint.

code.description: Machine-readable code — clients branch on this, not on `message`.

details.description: Optional structured payload (field path, offending value, etc.). Shape is error-specific; carried as untyped JSON so the API crate does not need to enumerate every possibility.

ApiErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error taxonomy.

Any variant added here must also be assigned an HTTP status in [`http_status`]. The compiler enforces exhaustiveness.

oneOf.description: The `game` field in a request did not name a registered game.
An `agents[_]` entry did not name a registered agent kind.
The `config` blob failed validation against the target game's config schema.
The requested run id was not found (or has been evicted).
The requested game id / log file was not found.
An `offset` or `limit` query parameter was negative, zero where positive is required, or exceeds server-enforced ceilings.
An unexpected server-side failure. The `message` is safe to show users; `details` (if populated) is meant for operators.

The endpoint is scaffolded but not yet implemented. Used for routes shipped as stubs ahead of their full implementation (e.g. `/api/reports` in Unit 17, proper implementation deferred to a later unit).

`POST .../actions` was submitted with a `prompt_id` that does not match the currently-pending prompt. The game advanced before the submission landed. Fetch the latest `turn_prompt` via the SSE stream and retry with the new `prompt_id`. Phase 2.5.
`POST .../actions` supplied an `action_index` outside the range of the pending prompt's `legal_actions`. Phase 2.5.
`POST .../actions` arrived with no prompt pending for this seat — either the game has not reached the seat yet or the last prompt was already satisfied. Phase 2.5.
`POST .../actions` targeted a seat that is not backed by an `http-remote` agent. AI-only seats cannot be driven via HTTP. Phase 2.5.
A `POST /api/runs` payload named an agent kind that is CLI-only in the current phase — today `llm` and `stdio`. Server callers must use `playtest play --agents ...` from the command line. Phase 3.

ApiResponse_for_AnyValue.description:
Uniform envelope wrapping every JSON response the server emits.

The envelope guarantees two things to consumers:

1. `api_version` is always present — clients can refuse to parse a response whose major version differs from what they compiled against. 2. Errors share one shape across every endpoint — success is `data: Some(..), errors: []`, failure is `data: None, errors: [..]`. Partial success (e.g. batch validation) is `data: Some(..), errors: [..]`.

api_version.description: The wire-contract version this response conforms to. Always equal to [`crate::API_VERSION`] at send time.

data.description: The endpoint-specific payload, if the request succeeded (fully or partially).

errors.description: Zero or more errors. Empty on full success; populated on partial success or outright failure.

CreateRunRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /runs`.

`config` is carried as untyped JSON so this crate stays game-agnostic; the server parses it against the named game's schema before accepting the run.

agents.description: Ordered list of agent kind ids, one per seat. Length must fall within the target game's declared player-count range (e.g. exactly 2 for Cribbage, 2-4 for ShipWreck).

config.description: Game-specific configuration blob. Shape is defined by the target game's `config_schema` (see [`crate::registry::GameRegistryEntry`]).

games_count.description: How many games to play in this run. Must be >= 1.

seed.description: Optional base seed. `None` means "pick one at run start".

EventPage.description: Paginated page of log lines returned by `GET /games/:id/events`.

events.description: The page's records, in on-disk order.

limit.description: Maximum page size that was requested.

offset.description: Zero-based offset of the first record in `events`.

total.description: Total number of records in the log (header + events + final).

GameMetadata.description: Full metadata row returned by `GET /games/:id`. Mirrors the JSON contents of a log's header plus a few server-side additions.

agents.description: Agent kind ids, one per seat, from the header.

config_hash.description: Hex-encoded hash of the game config.

finished_at.description: Wall-clock time the game finished, Unix epoch milliseconds. `None` if the log has no `Final` record (crashed mid-play).

id.description: Stable game id (usually derived from log filename).

run_id.description: Run id this game belongs to, if known.

scores.description: Final scores per seat, if the game ended cleanly.

seed.description: Base seed the run was started with.

started_at.description: Wall-clock time the game started, Unix epoch milliseconds.

version.description: Engine/build version stamped at write time.

winner.description: Winning player seat, if the game ended cleanly.

config_schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape of this game's `config` blob. Carried as raw JSON so the API crate does not have to depend on any particular schema library at runtime.

finished_at.description: Wall-clock time the game finished, Unix epoch milliseconds. `None` if the log has no `Final` record (crashed mid-play).

id.description: Stable game id (usually derived from log filename).

run_id.description: Run id this game belongs to, if known.

started_at.description: Wall-clock time the game started, Unix epoch milliseconds.

winner.description: Winning player seat, if the game ended cleanly.

LogLineDto.description: One record from an event log, carried to the client as the already-serialized JSON object. Using `JsonValue` keeps the API crate game-agnostic — the exact shape of `event.payload` is defined by the game crate that produced the log.

kind.description: Kind discriminant as it appears on the JSONL line (`"header"`, `"event"`, or `"final"`).

line.description: The full JSON object for this line. Callers parse this against the game's event type to recover typed values.

oneOf.description: Accepted by the server but not yet started.
Currently executing games.
All games finished successfully.
Terminated early due to an error.

agents.description: Agent kind ids, one per seat.

created_at.description: Wall-clock time the run was created, Unix epoch milliseconds.

finished_at.description: Wall-clock time the run finished, Unix epoch milliseconds. `None` while `status` is `Pending` or `Running`.

game.description: Registered game id this run is playing.

games_completed.description: Games that have finished (successfully or not) so far.

seed.description: Base seed chosen for the run.

SseFrame.description:
One frame in an SSE stream.

Serialized with `#[serde(tag = "kind", content = "data")]`, so the JSON shape is `{"kind":"event","data":{...}}` / `{"kind":"heartbeat"}` / etc.

oneOf.description: First frame on every stream. `data` is the JSON object for the log's header record.
An in-progress game event. `data` is the JSON object for one `Event` record from the log.
Last frame when a game ends cleanly. `data` is the JSON object for the log's `Final` record.

A remote agent is waiting for a submission. Ephemeral — not in the JSONL log, not resumable via `Last-Event-ID`. On reconnect the server re-emits this frame from the coordinator's pending state when the game is still waiting.
Keep-alive tick so proxies do not time out idle streams. Carries no payload.

SubmitActionBody.description: Body of `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/games/{game_id}/actions` — the inbound path Phase 2.5 introduces for browser-driven play.

action_index.description: Zero-based index into the prompt's `legal_actions` list.

prompt_id.description: The `prompt_id` from the `turn_prompt` frame being answered. Prevents stale submissions after the game has advanced.

seat.description: Zero-based seat index the action is for. Must match the seat of the currently-pending prompt.

SubmitActionResponse.description: Response body of a successful action submission. Minimal by design — the next `event` frame on the SSE stream is the meaningful signal that the submission was applied.

accepted.description: Always `true` on a 200 response; kept so the shape is a JSON object rather than a bare `null`.

TurnPromptPayload.description: Payload carried by [`SseFrame::TurnPrompt`]. A remote agent at `seat` is waiting for a submission; the client should POST an action_index into the legal list. Echo `prompt_id` back so the server can reject stale submissions.

legal_actions.description: Legal actions indexed 0..N, each serialized as the game's `Action` type. The client picks one index and submits it.

prompt_id.description: Per-game monotonic id; echo on submission so the server can reject stale prompts (e.g., the game advanced before the client submitted).

seat.description: Zero-based seat index the prompt is addressed to.

post.description: Inbound path for browser-driven play. The body carries `{seat, prompt_id, action_index}`. The server validates against the pending prompt on the per-game `TurnCoordinator`: seat must have a registered `http-remote` agent, a prompt must be pending for that seat, the submitted `prompt_id` must match, and `action_index` must be in range. Success returns 200 with `{accepted: true}`. The next `event` frame on the SSE stream is the real signal that the action was applied.
post.summary: Submit an action_index for a pending turn_prompt (Phase 2.5).

get.description: Returns a window of records from the game's JSONL log. Records are returned in on-disk order: header, zero or more events, then a final record (if the game ended cleanly). Use `offset` + `limit` to page forward; the response's `total` field is the current line count of the log.

parameters.description: Max records in the page (1..=10000). Default 100.
parameters.name: limit

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream. On connect the server replays any events up to the current tail of the on-disk log, then switches to the live feed. Reconnecting clients SHOULD send `Last-Event-ID: <tick>`; the server will skip any tick id less than or equal to that value. Each `event:`-typed frame carries its tick as the frame's SSE `id`. `heartbeat` frames carry no tick.

parameters.description: Tick id of the last `event`-typed SSE frame the client received. On reconnect the server skips any frame with a tick id <= this value.
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

200.description: Infinite SSE stream of `SseFrame` values. Ends on the first `final` frame.

get.summary: Live SSE stream of a game's log.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Frames fire when games inside this run start and finish, plus one terminal `run_complete` frame. Clients may reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` but run-level frames are not re-delivered — use the per-game stream for replay semantics.

200.description: Infinite SSE stream of `{game_started, game_finished, run_complete}` frames.
